A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NestQuant, with matching authors, core algorithms and original experiments. All 16 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support matching text, equations, figures and tables across relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-matrix simulations, Llama perplexity and zero-shot evaluations, and quantization ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds larger-model evaluations, activation-noise diagnostics, NestQuantM results and GPU kernel timings.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 introduces QA-LDLQ, replacing ordinary LDLQ with transformed weights and a Hessian incorporating activation-noise covariance. Appendix D adds NestQuantM, whose decoder repairs parity using a fixed coordinate instead of argmin/argmax searches while retaining the original encoding oracle. These change the quantization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText2, ARC-Easy/Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande and synthetic Gaussian matrix data. The added Llama configurations, precision settings and GEMV timings extend evaluation within the retained language and matrix-product tasks; they do not introduce another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds reported comparisons with QuIP#, OstQuant and DuQuant, and includes QuaRot in weight-only comparisons. Appendix E.1 adds kernel comparisons with QuIP# and uniform int4. The original Table 1 comparator set remains, so these are substantive extensions rather than renamed or replaced baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-2 7B/13B/70B and Llama-3-70B configurations, W3A3KV16 evaluation with q=7 and k=4, and an 8192-by-8192 GEMV benchmark on an A100. Its noise diagnostic adds an epsilon sweep using ten 2048-token sequences. Existing WikiText2 split, context and calibration settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a substantial failure analysis: poor Llama-3-70B quantization is traced to four activation-sensitive layers, with a full-precision-layer intervention and Figure 6 examining the noise-amplification versus output-error tradeoff. The earlier LDLQ, rotation, scaling-count and First-beta/Opt-beta analyses remain, including those relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new activation-noise covariance model and epsilon sweep concern the method and sensitivity analysis, rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive result entries, including Llama-3-70B full-quantization perplexity of 3.61 in Table 2 and three-bit results in Appendix J. Table 4 reports NestQuantM at 60 microseconds versus 97 for FP16 and 31 for uniform int4; the approximately 75-microsecond QuIP# four-bit value is extrapolated. Original benchmark and ablation tables retain their values.

T1.justification: v2 adds Lemma 4.2 and its QA-LDLQ derivation under independent, zero-mean activation noise, plus Lemma D.1 proving translation equivariance of the modified oracle. It also introduces the amplification-ratio definition and NestQuantM shaping argument. The earlier crude runtime derivation is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and results summary expand the headline comparison from primarily Llama-3-8B versus SpinQuant to claimed uniform superiority across models through 70B. Section 1.1 identifies QA-LDLQ as an innovation and claims full quantization can outperform prior methods retaining full-precision KV caches. The original drop-in quantizer claim and 6.6-perplexity example remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds activation-noise amplification as a large-model failure mechanism and explains QA-LDLQ's tradeoff between noise robustness and output bias. It also explains NestQuantM's altered shaping region and qualifies the comparison against W4A4KV16 methods with a Llama-2-7B exception. These extend v1's interpretations centered on lattice shaping and ordinary LDLQ.

D1.justification: Appendix E replaces the earlier operation-count discussion with concrete CUDA implementation information: an integer basis for 2E8, packed vector representations, bit-mask operations, beta-index decoding and code listings. Hardware and kernel-benchmark details are added. The original calibration and beta-search disclosures remain in relocated Appendix G.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to lattice quantization noise, Optimal Brain Compression, DuQuant and OstQuant, and positions QA-LDLQ as a correction to LDLQ/GPTQ when activations are quantized. The existing information-theoretic and LLM-quantization survey remains largely intact; many other reference edits only update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The overall introduction–prior work–method–experiments structure and much of the prose remain. v2 rewrites the codebook explanation and results summary, clarifies terminology, and moves the Llama-3.2-1B and scaling-count discussions into appendices. This is targeted editing and reorganization rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds a central multi-model comparison table, kernel-timing and three-bit tables, and a paired noise-amplification figure. Figure 4 corrects the Hadamard/output-projection order. Existing Llama-3.2-1B and scaling-count displays move to appendices, while the other original plots are retained. Together these substantially extend the evidence displays.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's practical case: QA-LDLQ responds to a documented large-model failure, Table 2 validates configurations through 70B, and Appendix E supplies CUDA code and measured kernel timings where v1 mainly offered cost estimates. These substantially strengthen applicability and reproducibility. Some superiority wording exceeds the tables, including a QuIP# tie, and the timing comparison uses unequal bitrates and an extrapolated baseline; these limitations do not outweigh the gains.
